capabilities: Display a Word-like formatting toolbar in top or cursor-following position
Run built-in commands for font/background color, headings, alignment, lists, and fullscreen focus
Customize the toolbar with custom icons, renamed commands, submenus, and drag-and-drop sorting
Apply formatting brushes for font and background colors
Use AI-assisted rewrite and inline completion via a user-configured API endpoint
extras: The README includes a privacy/network-access section: AI requests go to a user-configured endpoint, optional PKMer sync talks to api.pkmer.cn, and it states vault contents are not transmitted. Installation instructions and a video introduction are linked externally.
intentEvidence: The Editing Toolbar is modified from cMenu, which provides more powerful customization settings
motivation: The author re-modified the cMenu plugin because it had not been maintained for over a year, adding a top toolbar, cursor-following, and other new features.
problem: Obsidian relies on hotkeys and multi-key Markdown commands for formatting, which is hard for users who want a rich-text, WYSIWYG-like editing experience.
